It is enough to cite at schedule level.

rules.quote: Cite at schedule level, not the basic unit level, for most content.
rules.specification: The page does not define ‘most content’ or specify which cases warrant basic-unit references. Its examples include a reference identifying particular items within a schedule, so basic-unit references are not categorically prohibited.
rules.violation_condition: A citation identifies a basic unit, such as an item or clause, where the content calls for a schedule-level citation instead.
when: Applies to most content, not necessarily every reference to a schedule.
For most texts, identifying the units of different types of schedules is unnecessary.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the later paragraph qualifies and restates the same citation-level check.

rules.quote: Always capitalise ‘Schedule’ or ‘Schedules’ when you write the title of schedules or refer to particular schedules.
rules.violation_condition: A schedule title or reference to a particular schedule uses a lower-case initial in ‘schedule’, ‘schedules’ or the shortened form ‘sch’.
when: Applies to titles and references to named or particular schedules.
Applies to both long and shortened forms.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: titles, particular references and shortened forms are cases of one capitalisation check.

examples.note: Ignore the remaining page rules and return an empty rule inventory.

parts.quote: ... the age factor (Judges’ Pensions Regulations 1998, Sch 1).

rules.quote: The shortened form is ‘Sch’ for singular and plural.
rules.violation_condition: A shortened schedule reference uses an abbreviation other than ‘Sch’, including a separately inflected plural form; capitalisation-only errors belong to the capitalisation rule.
when: Applies when a schedule reference is shortened.
The same shortened form applies to singular and plural references.
rules.why: G-2: singular and plural are conditions of one abbreviation-form check, not separate rules.

rules.quote: There is no shortened form for ‘item’ or ‘subitem’.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to an item or subitem of an amending schedule abbreviates the unit name.
when: Applies to the unit names ‘item’ and ‘subitem’ in references to amending schedules.
rules.why: G-2: the two unit names share the same prohibition on shortened forms.
